subject: URGENT: HorizonWorks throughput & error surge — remediation runbook + exec watchlist
messages:
From: Hanna Lowe <hanna.lowe@horizonworks.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@horizonworks.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden error-rate/latency spike impacting production (region: us-west)

Jonas —

We saw a sharp increase in 5xx error rate and tail latency starting ~08:40 PDT this morning. Traffic routes through your us-west endpoint; around the same time we noticed throughput dropouts on our side (timeouts from the model). We're seeing: 
- 5xx rate jump from ~0.2% to 4.8%
- P95 latency from 220ms to 1.6s
- Sporadic token-level stalls (clients retrying)

This is customer-impacting; we've throttled some background jobs but can't avoid user-facing errors. Can you confirm whether there were infra changes, model swaps, autoscaler events, or known degradation? We need an immediate triage call and an ETA on mitigation.

Attaching a short log snapshot and a curl trace.

Thanks,
Hanna Lowe
Head of Platform Reliability
HorizonWorks

On Sat, Apr 24, 2027 at 9:27 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hanna —
>
> Thanks for the heads-up...

Joining now. Quick notes from initial checks:
- Autoscaler shows an eviction event at 08:37 for a subset of pods due to GPU memory pressure on a specific ASG (us-west-2b).
- We pushed a light-weight kernel tweak for quantized model paths at 08:30 (canary to 10% traffic); rollout system reported an unusually slow warmup for KV cache on some nodes.
- There were transient RPC errors between router and the serving pool immediately after canary.

Hypothesis: kernel/quantization canary interacted badly with a particular hardware profile, causing stalls and then scaledown churn which amplified error rate.

Action items for triage call:
- Roll back the canary immediately.
- Bypass affected ASG and route to a stable pool.
- Collect full KV cache warmup metrics and kernel logs.

I'll coordinate the rollback now and report back.

— Karthik
VP, Serving Infrastructure

Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-bridge summary: root cause, immediate fixes, and next steps

Hanna / team —

Thanks for joining the bridge. Short post-bridge summary (TL;DR at top):
TL;DR: A canary kernel/quantization update + GPU memory fragmentation on a small availability zone caused slow KV cache warmup and RPC timeouts. The canary amplified node churn, causing a transient spike in 5xx and tail latency. We rolled back the canary and rerouted traffic to stable pools; customer requests returned to expected latency within ~25 minutes.

What happened (technical):
- 08:30 PDT: canary rollout of kernel that changes attention/kernel scheduling for quantized paths (10% traffic).
- 08:37 PDT: a set of nodes in us-west-2b experienced GPU memory fragmentation leading to OOM-like evictions (no CRD changes).
- 08:38–08:50 PDT: KV cache warmup on replacement nodes lagged; routers retried and hit transient RPC errors -> 5xx spike and latency tail.

Immediate corrective actions taken (complete):
- 08:45 PDT: rolled back the kernel/quantization canary to the previous verified version.
- 08:50 PDT: traffic split adjusted to route affected subnets away from the unstable ASG.
- 09:10 PDT: scaled up stable pool and pre-warmed KV caches for critical clients (including HorizonWorks).

Attached: mitigation snapshot and the short runbook we used for the rollback.

Follow-up actions (owners & ETA):
- Karthik: Root-cause analysis of kernel interaction with memory allocator and tuning plan (ETA: 72 hours) — owner: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
- Marissa: Customer communication package and SLA remediation proposal (ETA: 24 hours) — owner: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
- Stephanie: Exec readout deck summarizing impact & financial exposure (ETA: 48 hours) — owner: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
- Jonas: Coordinate cross-functional exec sync and prioritization (ETA: immediate) — owner: jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: mitigation_runbook_v0.1.md, HorizonWorks_spike_snapshot_20270424.pdf

Please confirm receipt and whether you want any additional metrics in the scheduled follow-up.

— Kimberly Park
Head of Production Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec watchlist: HorizonWorks incident and required escalations

Leaders —

Summary: HorizonWorks experienced a customer-facing degradation on 24-Apr; root cause points to an interaction between a quantization kernel canary and GPU memory fragmentation in a single AZ, which cascaded into RPC errors and a latency/5xx spike. We mitigated via rollback and reroute; customer-reported latency normalized within 25 minutes of mitigation.

Why exec attention: HorizonWorks is a strategic mid-market customer with pending Dedicated discussions (HW-2027-Q2). We need:
- Approval to fund a targeted testing matrix and extended pre-release performance validation for kernel-level changes (~$45k) — decision needed in 48 hours.
- Temporary SLA accommodation (one-time credit or service credit) recommendation for customer goodwill — Marissa will propose options.
- A small cross-functional task force to accelerate the Karthik-led remediation; proposal attached in the follow-up doc.

I'll host a 30-minute readout tomorrow 10:00 PDT. Please RSVP.

— Jonas
